## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-dsc-definition

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: definition of historical DSC, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Historical debt service coverage is EBITDA divided by all debt service after the transaction, not only the SBA loan payment.
- **Quote:** "The historical DSC ratio is defined as earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (EBITDA) divided by the combined debt service post-transaction."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-lease-term

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 3: lease term when the borrower leases space, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** Where this paragraph applies, the lender must get a copy of the lease, and for 7(a) loans the lease term including the borrower's renewal options should equal or exceed the loan term.
- **Quote:** "The SBA Lender must obtain a copy of the written lease between the Borrower and the landlord. For 7(a) loans, the lease term, including renewal options exercisable only by the Borrower, should equal or exceed the term of the loan."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-partial-seller-stays

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller may stay in a partial change, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In an SBA partial change of ownership (an owner buyout), the selling owner may stay on as an owner or employee.
- **Quote:** "The seller may stay on as an owner, officer, director, stockholder, Key Employee, or employee of the business."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-professional-license-ownership

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 2: businesses needing professional licenses, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** A business whose services require a professional license is SBA-eligible only if its ownership structure meets the state's requirements.
- **Quote:** "Businesses that offer services which require professional licenses to operate are eligible, provided that the ownership structure meets all applicable state requirements in which they are located."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-projections

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15, Para. C.2: projections, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In a 7(a) change of ownership the lender may not rely on projections to meet the coverage requirement, except for an owner-occupied special purpose property.
- **Quote:** "The Lender must evaluate the Applicant's post-closing financial projections but may not rely on them to meet the DSC requirement. This limitation does not apply to a transaction involving the acquisition of an owner-occupied Special Purpose Property, which may be underwritten on the basis of projections as provided under Special Purpose Properties above."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26

## sba-sop-50-10-8-1-seller-consultant

- **Source:** SOP 50 10 8.1, Appendix 15: seller may stay only as a consultant, up to 24 months, U.S. Small Business Administration
- **URL:** https://legacy.sba.gov/sites/default/files/2026-10/SOP%2050%2010%208.1%20Technical%20Policy%20Updates%20effective%20%2010.1.2026.docx
- **Supports:** In an SBA 7(a) initial acquisition or business expansion, the seller can't stay as an officer, director, owner or employee, but the business may hire the seller as a consultant for up to 24 months in total.
- **Quote:** "Except as provided below, the seller in a Business Expansion or Initial Acquisition change of ownership transaction may not remain as an officer, director, stockholder, or employee of the business. If a transitional period is needed to assist the business, the small business may contract with the seller as a consultant for a period not to exceed 24 months (in aggregate, including any extensions)."
- **Checked:** 2026-11-26 · **Re-check by:** 2027-02-26
